Reproducing Holdgraf et al. (2016) from CRCNS ac-4¶

Paper: Holdgraf, de Heer, Pasley, Rieger, Crone, Lin, Knight & Theunissen (2016), "Rapid tuning shifts in human auditory cortex enhance speech intelligibility", Nat Commun 7:13654, doi:10.1038/ncomms13654.

Dataset: CRCNS ac-4 (doi:10.6080/K08S4N4J), "Electrocorticography recordings from patients during a passive listening task of degraded and intact English speech", read in place from ac-4/live/data.zip in the public S3 bucket crcnsarchive.

Version: CRCNS data sets are not versioned, so the version is recorded as unversioned. The bucket holds one copy of the data set (ac-4/live/, no old/ folder), the data descriptor's version 0.6 of 28 May 2019, which is the only published version and the one the paper's data availability statement points to. The MD5 of data.zip in the data set's checksums.md5 is printed below, so a later change is detectable.

Claims: claims/crcns-ac-4/10.1038-ncomms13654.yaml, written from the version of record with its Supplementary Information. The claims file decides what is tested; method details it lacks are taken from the paper and cited where they are used (in this notebook or in ac4.py).

Claim Tested here
behav-no-context-baseline, behav-context-enhancement, supp1a-linguistic-context, supp1a-speaker-no-difference, supp1b-filter-type, supp5a-behaviour-over-trials Blocked: the behavioural control data are not in the data set
speech-r-count Tested
fig3b-hfb-increase-after Tested
supp3a-pink-noise-no-hfb-change Tested
supp5b-hfb-stable-over-session Tested
fig4a-coherence-after-higher, fig4b-coherence-sentence-specific Tested
strf-r-count, included-electrode-count Tested
fig8-mtf-matches-filter Tested
fig9-rms-increase, fig9-middle-generalizes-after Tested
fig10-partial-correlation, fig10b-similarity-correlates, fig10c-stg-location Tested
supp3b-pink-noise-no-pcorr-change Run, but no electrode of the pink noise subjects is included, so it is blocked
supp6a-connectivity-increase, supp6a-after-closer-to-middle, supp6b-no-pac-change Tested
supp7-envelope-coherence Tested
supp4-hfb-power-increase Tested

The whole notebook streams about 1.6 GB and takes about 25 minutes, about half of it loading.

Revised after the first verification round: supp5b runs under the three z-scores with a bootstrap that resamples whole sounds or subjects; the coherence of fig4, supp6a and supp7 uses MNE's default multitaper half-bandwidth (NW = 4, seven tapers; claims, open detail 10), with the earlier choices as variants; supp6a uses all included electrodes as seeds, as the criterion says; the spectrogram and the HFB are checked for alignment; fig8 adds a region rule from the filter cutoffs; PAC leaves an electrode out of its own phase mean; supp4 adds power without a baseline.

# LOAD: stream each subject, reduce it to HFB at 50 Hz, the auditory spectrograms and speech
# envelopes of every sound, and the re-referenced signal around each sound (see ac4.load_subject)
t0 = time.time()
z = ac4.open_zip()
D = {}
for s in ac4.SUBJECTS:
    D[s] = ac4.load_subject(z, s)
    print(s, f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s", f"peak memory {resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1e6:.1f} GB")

def region(desc):
    if desc.startswith("temporal") or desc == "sub_temporal":
        return "temporal"
    if desc.endswith("-inferior"):
        return "perisylvian"          # inferior frontal, premotor, motor, parietal
    if desc.startswith("frontal") or desc.startswith("premotor"):
        return "frontal"
    return "other"

rows = []
for s, d in D.items():
    ch, tr, js = d["channels"], d["trials"], d["json"]
    rows.append(dict(subject=s, channels=len(ch), good=int((ch.status == "good").sum()),
                     fs=js["SamplingFrequency"], duration_json=js["RecordingDuration"],
                     duration_samples=d["stats"]["n_samples"] / ac4.FS,
                     audio_sr=d["audio_sr"], audio_s=d["audio_len"] / d["audio_sr"],
                     triplets=tr.loc[tr.trial_num >= 0, "trial_num"].nunique(),
                     noise_triplets=tr.loc[tr.noise, "trial_num"].nunique(),
                     lone_unfiltered=int((tr.trial_num < 0).sum()),
                     sound_s=f"{tr.duration.min():.2f}-{tr.duration.max():.2f}",
                     bad_spans=int((d["events"].trial_type == "bad").sum()),
                     sounds_overlapping_bad=int(tr.overlaps_bad.sum()),
                     raw_abs_median=d["stats"]["raw_abs_median"],
                     car_residual=d["stats"]["car_residual"]))
summary = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(summary.to_string())

for s, d in D.items():

The checks above, stated:

  • Sampling rate 1000 Hz in every ieeg.json, and sample counts give the stated recording durations (columns duration_json and duration_samples).
  • The stored values are not in the stated millivolts: the median absolute value is about 300 in S01 and 1.7e8 to 6.2e8 in the other subjects. The analysis uses only z-scored or normalized measures, so the scale does not enter any result; it is recorded as a finding.
  • The good channels are already re-referenced to their common average (the mean over good channels is about 1e-8 of the signal), as channels.tsv says (CAR).
  • The paper reports 7 subjects with grids of 48, 64, 68, 68, 62, 110 and 104 channels and 468 electrodes kept; the data set has 7 subjects with 416 channels, 377 marked good.
  • Three subjects (S07, S08, S13) have pink noise triplets, about half of their triplets, as the paper says.

Clock checks follow: the audio track against the event onsets, and the HFB against the onsets, with the onsets shifted as the contrast.

# HFB clock check: on temporal electrodes, mean HFB 0.1-0.5 s after onset minus -0.4-0 s,
# at the true onsets and at onsets shifted by -2 to +2 s
shifts = np.arange(-2.0, 2.01, 0.1)
for s, d in D.items():
    temp = (d["good"].description.map(region) == "temporal").to_numpy()
    h = d["hfb"][temp]
    on = d["trials"].onset.to_numpy()
    con = []
    for sh in shifts:
        i = np.round((on + sh) * ac4.FS_OUT).astype(int)
        post = np.mean([h[:, j + 5:j + 25].mean() for j in i])
        pre = np.mean([h[:, j - 20:j].mean() for j in i])
        con.append((post - pre) / h.std())
    con = np.array(con)
    ax[1].plot(shifts, con, lw=0.8)
    print(s, f"HFB contrast at true onsets {con[np.argmin(np.abs(shifts))]:.3f}; largest at shift {shifts[np.argmax(con)]:+.1f} s; range {con.min():.3f} to {con.max():.3f}")
ax[1].set(xlabel="onset shift (s)", ylabel="HFB post minus pre (s.d.)", title="HFB at shifted onsets")
plt.tight_layout()

Electrode selection (Speech-R)¶

Methods, Evoked HFB and speech-responsive electrodes: each trial baselined at -800 to -100 ms, the mean post-stimulus activity per trial, a bootstrap 99% interval of the mean over trials, and Speech-R when its 0.5th percentile is above 0 in response to unfiltered speech. The claims file names three open details (1 trials, 2 window, 3 z-score); every combination is run.

Triplets with pink noise are left out of every speech analysis (Figure 3 heading "MIDDLE (context) unfiltered speech only"). The six unfiltered sentences outside any triplet in S01 to S04 (trial number -1) are left out too: they are not MIDDLE sounds of the task.

speech-r-count: 92 of the 468 electrodes (19.6%) responded to speech above baseline (Speech-R), generally centred on perisylvian regions.

readings = []
for zmode in ["trial", "pooled", "nonevent"]:
    for win in ["sound", "2.5"]:
        for tsel in ["mid", "all"]:
            lbs = []
            for s, d in D.items():
                ep, times = EP[s]
                tr = d["trials"]
                zep = ac4.zscore_epochs(d, ep, times, zmode)
                pm = ac4.post_mean(zep, times, tr.duration.to_numpy(), win)
                POST[(s, zmode, win)] = pm
                sel = (tr.trial_num >= 0) & ~tr.noise
                if tsel == "mid":
                    sel &= tr.trial_phase == "mid"
                lbs.append(ac4.bootstrap_lower(pm[sel.to_numpy()], rng))
            lb = np.concatenate(lbs)
            E[f"lb_{zmode}_{win}_{tsel}"] = lb
            n = int((lb > 0).sum())
            readings.append(dict(zscore=zmode, window=win, trials=tsel, speech_r=n,
                                 pct_of_good=100 * n / len(E), within_92_tol=abs(n - 92) <= 9.2,
                                 **{s: int((lb[E.subject.eq(s).to_numpy()] > 0).sum()) for s in D}))

The reading carried into the later claims is the z-score by non-event times (the code's zscore_by_non_events), the 0 to 2.5 s window, and MIDDLE trials (the Methods): of the readings within the paper's count, it is the first in the order the claims file lists them. Only the non-event z-score gives counts near the paper's; see the record's assumptions. Sounds that overlap a span marked bad in the events table are kept, as the paper does not mention such spans (column sounds_overlapping_bad above).

Result: speech-r-count. Three of the twelve readings give a count within 92 +/- 9.2, all with the z-score by non-event times: 96 (onset to sound end, all speech trials), 101 (0 to 2.5 s, MIDDLE trials) and 99 (0 to 2.5 s, all trials). The z-score by each trial's own baseline or by the pooled baseline gives 131 to 185. The data set holds 377 good electrodes (416 in all), against the paper's 468, so 101 is 26.8% of the electrodes against the paper's 19.6%. Speech-R electrodes lie mostly on temporal (66) and perisylvian (18) sites. The count is reproduced under the non-event z-score; the electrode total differs.

HFB increase AFTER against BEFORE¶

fig3b-hfb-increase-after: Across Speech-R electrodes, HFB activity is higher in the AFTER condition than in the BEFORE condition (cluster-based permutation test, P = 0.003, n = 92).

Per electrode, the trial-averaged AFTER minus BEFORE time course of z-scored HFB (Methods, Evoked HFB: "the difference in time-varying HFB activity in each trial was calculated and then averaged across trials"), from -0.5 to 3 s (the Figure 3b axis), and MNE's one-sample cluster permutation test across electrodes (claims, open detail 11: default threshold, 10,000 permutations).

In [6]:
def diff_timecourse(zmode, sel_fn, t0=-0.5, t1=3.0):
    """(electrodes, time) of mean AFTER minus mean BEFORE z-HFB, for the electrodes of E in order."""
    out = []
    for s, d in D.items():
        ep, times = EP[s]
        zep = ac4.zscore_epochs(d, ep, times, zmode)
        tr = d["trials"]
        keep = (times >= t0) & (times <= t1)
        b = sel_fn(tr) & (tr.trial_phase == "bef")
        a = sel_fn(tr) & (tr.trial_phase == "aft")
        out.append(zep[a.to_numpy()][..., keep].mean(0) - zep[b.to_numpy()][..., keep].mean(0))
    return np.concatenate(out), times[keep]

def as_mask(cl, shape):
    m = np.zeros(shape, bool)
    m[cl] = True
    return m

def clusters_of(X, seed, n_perm=10000):
    """MNE's one-sample cluster permutation test (default threshold, two-tailed); masks."""
    T, clusters, pv, _ = mne.stats.permutation_cluster_1samp_test(X, n_permutations=n_perm, tail=0, seed=seed, out_type="mask")
    return T, [as_mask(c, X.shape[1:]) for c in clusters], pv

def cluster_report(X, label, seed, times=None, n_perm=10000):
    T, clusters, pv = clusters_of(X, seed, n_perm)
    rows = []
    for c, p in zip(clusters, pv):
        idx = np.where(c)[0] if c.ndim == 1 else None
        rows.append(dict(set=label, n=X.shape[0], p=p, sign="+" if T[c].mean() > 0 else "-",
                         start=None if idx is None or times is None else times[idx[0]],
                         end=None if idx is None or times is None else times[idx[-1]],
                         size=int(c.sum())))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows) if rows else pd.DataFrame([dict(set=label, n=X.shape[0], p=np.nan, sign="none", start=None, end=None, size=0)])

speech = lambda tr: (tr.trial_num >= 0) & ~tr.noise
out = []
for zmode in ["nonevent", "trial"]:
    DIF, tt = diff_timecourse(zmode, speech)
    for label, m in [("(a) all Speech-R", E.speech_r), ("(b) Speech-R temporal+perisylvian", E.speech_r & E.region.isin(["temporal", "perisylvian"]))]:

HFB over the session¶

supp5b-hfb-stable-over-session: Mean HFB activity of Speech-R electrodes shows no significant relation to trial number over a session.

The paper's test is a bootstrap of the regression slope on trial number (ecogtools bootstrap_coefficients, 1000 resamples, as the claims file gives it). The value is the mean post-stimulus HFB of each speech sound (all three phases, 0 to 2.5 s), and trial number the triplet number. Two units, as the criterion names: (a) every Speech-R electrode's value per sound, pooled; (b) the mean over Speech-R electrodes per sound and subject. The z-score is open (claims, open detail 3), and the z-score by non-event times is fixed over the session, so a slow drift appears as a slope, while a per-trial baseline removes it; all three readings are run. Values of one sound are not independent across electrodes, so unit (a) is also bootstrapped by resampling whole sounds, and unit (b) by resampling whole subjects.

In [8]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(505)
def boot_slope(x, y, rng, n=1000, groups=None):
    """Slope of y on x and its 95% bootstrap interval; with groups, whole groups are resampled."""
    x, y = np.asarray(x, float), np.asarray(y, float)
    slopes = np.empty(n)
    if groups is not None:
        ug, inv = np.unique(groups, return_inverse=True)
        members = [np.where(inv == k)[0] for k in range(len(ug))]
    for i in range(n):
        if groups is None:
            j = rng.integers(0, len(x), len(x))
        else:
            j = np.concatenate([members[k] for k in rng.integers(0, len(ug), len(ug))])
        slopes[i] = np.polyfit(x[j], y[j], 1)[0]
    return np.polyfit(x, y, 1)[0], np.percentile(slopes, [2.5, 97.5])

Result: supp5b-hfb-stable-over-session. The slope of HFB on trial number is negative under every z-score and unit, about -0.1 to -0.18 z over 57 triplets. With the adopted z-score by non-event times, the 95% interval excludes 0 for unit (a) whether pairs or whole sounds are resampled (-0.0032 to -0.0012 with sounds) and for unit (b) (-0.0029 to -0.0008); resampling whole subjects in unit (b) gives -0.0039 to 0.00001, which just includes 0. The pooled baseline z-score excludes 0 under all four bootstraps. The per-trial baseline z-score includes 0 under three of four (unit (a) with sounds resampled, -0.0056 to 0.0010; unit (b), -0.0063 to 0.0001) and excludes it under the fourth (unit (a) with pairs resampled, -0.0037 to -0.0005), and only one of seven subjects has an interval below 0 with it, against six of seven with the other two z-scores. The claim of absence is not reproduced under the adopted z-score, the one carried into every HFB claim; under the per-trial baseline the absence holds with the grouped bootstraps (sounds or subjects resampled) and not with pairs resampled, so the outcome rests on the z-score.

Between-condition coherence¶

fig4a-coherence-after-higher / fig4b-coherence-sentence-specific

Methods, Between-condition coherence: per sentence, the coherence of the HFB time course between BEFORE and MIDDLE and between AFTER and MIDDLE, in 400 ms windows stepped by 200 ms from -500 to 2500 ms, jackknife-corrected, converted to bits/s, averaged over trials; then the sign-flip test of AFTER/MIDDLE minus BEFORE/MIDDLE across electrodes for the ranges of Figure 4 (-1 to 0, 0 to 1, 1 to 2.5 s). The multitaper bandwidth is open (claims, open detail 10), whose standard choice is MNE's multitaper default: a normalized half-bandwidth of 4 (_compute_mt_params with bandwidth=None), which for a 20-sample window gives seven tapers with concentration above 0.9. That is the main reading; NW = 2 (three tapers, the first revision's choice) is a variant. The coherence is integrated over all frequencies from 2.5 to 25 Hz: 2.5 Hz (1 / 400 ms) is the lowest frequency the window resolves, read here as the claims file's "lowest resolved frequency". The tapers smooth the spectrum over plus or minus W = NW / 0.4 s (10 Hz at NW = 4, 5 Hz at NW = 2), so a variant integrates from W. A window belongs to a range when it lies wholly inside it, so the -1 to 0 s range has one window (-0.5 to -0.1 s); assigning windows by their centre, which lets the window from -0.3 to 0.1 s into the pre-stimulus range, is shown as a variant. Electrode sets: (a) Speech-R on temporal or perisylvian cortex, (b) all temporal or perisylvian electrodes. Panel b subtracts from each trial the electrode's mean time course, (a) over all trials of all three conditions, (b) per condition.

In [9]:
def complete_triplets(tr):
    """Speech triplets with one BEFORE, one MIDDLE and one AFTER sound."""
    t = tr[speech(tr)]
    g = t.groupby("trial_num").trial_phase.apply(lambda x: sorted(x) == ["aft", "bef", "mid"])
    return sorted(g.index[g])

WIN_STARTS = np.round(np.arange(-0.5, 2.1001, 0.2), 1)
WIN_CENTRES = WIN_STARTS + 0.2
def coherence_bits(subtract=None, nw=4.0, fmin=None):
    """(electrodes of E, 2 pairs, windows) mean over triplets of integrated coherence in bits/s."""
    out = []
    for s, d in D.items():
        ep, times = EP[s]
        zep = ac4.zscore_epochs(d, ep, times, MAIN[0])
        tr = d["trials"]
        tsel = speech(tr)
        trip = complete_triplets(tr)
        ix = {ph: [tr.index[(tr.trial_num == n) & (tr.trial_phase == ph)][0] for n in trip] for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]}
        X = {ph: zep[ix[ph]] for ph in ix}
        if subtract == "all":
            m = zep[tsel.to_numpy()].mean(0)
            X = {ph: X[ph] - m for ph in X}
        elif subtract == "condition":
            X = {ph: X[ph] - X[ph].mean(0) for ph in X}
        res = np.empty((zep.shape[1], 2, len(WIN_STARTS)))
        for w, ws in enumerate(WIN_STARTS):
            sel = (times >= ws - 1e-9) & (times < ws + 0.4 - 1e-9)
            for k, ph in enumerate(["bef", "aft"]):
                f, c = ac4.mt_coherence(X[ph][..., sel], X["mid"][..., sel], ac4.FS_OUT, nw=nw)
                res[:, k, w] = ac4.coh_to_bits(c, f, fmin=fmin).mean(0)
        out.append(res)
    return np.concatenate(out), f

def window_tests(C, mask, rng, label, assign="inside"):
    """Sign-flip tests per range of Figure 4. A window belongs to a range when it lies wholly
    inside it ("inside", the main reading) or when its centre does ("centre")."""
    rows = []
    for name, lo, hi in [("-1 to 0 s", -1, 0), ("0 to 1 s", 0, 1), ("1 to 2.5 s", 1, 2.5)]:
        if assign == "inside":
            w = (WIN_STARTS >= lo - 1e-9) & (WIN_STARTS + 0.4 <= hi + 1e-9)
        else:
            w = (WIN_CENTRES >= lo) & (WIN_CENTRES < (hi if hi < 2.5 else 2.6))
        diff = (C[mask][:, 1, w] - C[mask][:, 0, w]).mean(1)
        obs, p = ac4.signflip_test(diff, rng)
        rows.append(dict(set=label, window=name, assign=assign, n=int(mask.sum()), windows=int(w.sum()),
                         bef_mid=C[mask][:, 0, w].mean(), aft_mid=C[mask][:, 1, w].mean(),
                         diff=obs, se=diff.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(diff)), p=p))
    return rows

rng = np.random.default_rng(404)
peri = E.region.isin(["temporal", "perisylvian"]).to_numpy()
sets4 = {"(a) Speech-R temporal+perisylvian": peri & E.speech_r.to_numpy(), "(b) all temporal+perisylvian": peri}
COH4 = {nw: coherence_bits(None, nw) for nw in [4.0, 2.0]}
C4a, fr = COH4[4.0]
print("coherence frequencies (Hz):", fr)
rows = []
for nw, (C, _) in COH4.items():
    for assign in ["inside", "centre"]:
        for k, m in sets4.items():
            for r in window_tests(C, m, rng, k, assign):
                r["NW"] = nw
                rows.append(r)
for nw in [4.0, 2.0]:
    C, _ = coherence_bits(None, nw, fmin=nw / 0.4)
    for k, m in sets4.items():
        for r in window_tests(C, m, rng, k):
            r["NW"] = f"{nw:g}, from {nw / 0.4:g} Hz"
            rows.append(r)
R4a = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("windows per range (inside):", [int(((WIN_STARTS >= lo - 1e-9) & (WIN_STARTS + 0.4 <= hi + 1e-9)).sum()) for lo, hi in [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 2.5)]])

Result: fig4a-coherence-after-higher. With NW = 4, over the 84 Speech-R electrodes on temporal or perisylvian cortex, AFTER/MIDDLE coherence is higher than BEFORE/MIDDLE in both post-stimulus ranges (0 to 1 s: +0.80 bits/s, P = 0.0003; 1 to 2.5 s: +0.49 bits/s, P = 0.0004) and not before the sound (+0.31, P = 0.14). Assigning windows by centre gives the same (P = 0.0002, 0.0003; before the sound 0.82). Over all 251 temporal or perisylvian electrodes only the late range differs (P = 0.0003; 0 to 1 s P = 0.44). With NW = 2 set (a) also passes both ranges (P = 0.0012 and 0.013), but the pre-stimulus window differs too (P = 0.013), unlike the paper's 0.924. Five of seven subjects have a positive mean difference (S02 and S03 slightly negative). Integrated from W = 10 Hz, the lowest frequency the tapers resolve apart from 0 Hz, set (a) still passes both ranges (P = 0.013 and 0.0019) and not the pre-stimulus window (P = 0.21); NW = 2 integrated from 5 Hz keeps the NW = 2 pattern (P = 0.028 and 0.038; before the sound 0.014). Reproduced on the Speech-R set, under the claims file's standard bandwidth.

Result: fig4b-coherence-sentence-specific. With NW = 4, after subtracting the mean time course, the 1 to 2.5 s range still shows higher AFTER/MIDDLE coherence on the Speech-R set, with the mean over all trials subtracted (+0.29 bits/s, P = 0.0068) and with the mean per condition (+0.42, P = 0.0001). The 0 to 1 s range is not significant with the mean over all trials subtracted (P = 0.17, as in the paper, 0.241) and is with the mean per condition (P = 0.014). On all temporal or perisylvian electrodes the late range gives P = 0.015 and 0.0002. With NW = 2 the late range on the Speech-R set gives P = 0.11 (mean over all trials) and 0.012 (per condition). Integrated from W = 10 Hz at NW = 4, the late range still passes on the Speech-R set (P = 0.019 with the mean over all trials, 0.0099 per condition), and 0 to 1 s is then significant under both subtractions (P = 0.020 and 0.0087); NW = 2 from 5 Hz gives P = 0.18 and 0.043 for the late range. Reproduced on the Speech-R set under the standard bandwidth; with three tapers it holds under one of the two subtractions.

eSTRF fits¶

Methods, eSTRF model formulation: ridge regression of HFB on the auditory spectrogram at lags 0 to 400 ms, inputs and outputs z-scored (with the training trials' statistics here), one trial left out per split, R2 on the held-out trial; the ridge parameter is the mode of the per-split best values over active (Speech-R) electrodes and all conditions, and every model is re-fit with it; coefficients averaged over splits, and their mean over s.d. across splits where the paper says so. The ridge grid is a standard choice (log-spaced, 1 to 1e8), checked below to have its mode inside the grid. Samples per trial (claims, open detail 7): (a) onset to offset, the main reading; (b) onset to 400 ms after offset, run for the selection counts.

ALPHAS = np.logspace(0, 8, 17)
def cond_idx(tr, phase, noise=False, filt=None):
    sel = (tr.trial_num >= 0) & (tr.noise == noise) & (tr.trial_phase == phase)
    if filt is not None:
        sel &= tr.filt_type == filt
    return np.where(sel.to_numpy())[0]

t0 = time.time()
best, best_el = [], []
for s, d in D.items():
    sr = E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "speech_r"].to_numpy()
    for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]:
        Xs, ys = ac4.trial_design(d, cond_idx(d["trials"], ph))
        _, r2 = ac4.ridge_loto(Xs, ys, ALPHAS)
        best.append(ALPHAS[r2.argmax(1)][:, sr].ravel())
        best_el.append(ALPHAS[r2.mean(0).argmax(0)][sr])
best = np.concatenate(best)
vals, counts = np.unique(best, return_counts=True)
print(pd.Series(counts, index=[f"{v:.0e}" for v in vals]).to_string())
print(f"mode of all split values {vals[np.argmax(counts)]:.0e}, the top of the grid: in these splits no alpha predicts the held-out trial better than the null model")
inner = best[best < ALPHAS[-1]]
vals_i, counts_i = np.unique(inner, return_counts=True)
ALPHA = vals_i[np.argmax(counts_i)]
v_el, c_el = np.unique(np.concatenate(best_el), return_counts=True)
print(f"adopted: mode over split values below the top of the grid {ALPHA:.0e} ({len(inner)} of {len(best)} values)")
print(f"variant: mode of each electrode's best alpha (mean R2 over splits) {v_el[np.argmax(c_el)]:.0e}")
print(f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

FITS = {}
def fit(s, key, idx, window="sound"):
    d = D[s]
    Xs, ys = ac4.trial_design(d, idx, window)
    coefs, r2 = ac4.ridge_loto(Xs, ys, [ALPHA])
    coefs, r2 = coefs[:, 0], r2[:, 0]
    FITS[(s, key)] = dict(mean=coefs.mean(0), z=coefs.mean(0) / coefs.std(0), r2=r2, n_trials=len(idx))
t0 = time.time()
for s, d in D.items():
    tr = d["trials"]
    for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]:
        fit(s, ph, cond_idx(tr, ph))
    fit(s, "mid_plus", cond_idx(tr, "mid"), "plus")
    for ph in ["bef", "aft"]:
        for fl in ["temp", "freq"]:
            fit(s, f"{ph}_{fl}", cond_idx(tr, ph, filt=fl))
    if tr.noise.any():
        for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]:
            fit(s, f"noise_{ph}", cond_idx(tr, ph, noise=True))
print(f"fits done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
print(pd.DataFrame([dict(subject=s, fit=k, trials=v["n_trials"], median_r2=np.median(v["r2"])) for (s, k), v in FITS.items()]).pivot(index="subject", columns="fit", values="trials").to_string())

STRF-R electrodes¶

strf-r-count: 53 of 468 electrodes (11.3%) were well modelled by the eSTRF (STRF-R), generally on perisylvian temporal lobe.

Methods, STRF-responsive electrode selection: the lower bound of the R2 over cross-validation splits of the MIDDLE model above 0. Readings (claims, open detail 8): (a) 0.5th percentile of a bootstrap of the mean R2 over splits, (b) 1st percentile of the per-split R2, (c) 0.5th percentile of the per-split R2; with the samples of open detail 7, (a) and (b).

rows = []
for key, wlab in [("mid", "(a) onset-offset"), ("mid_plus", "(b) to offset+400 ms")]:
    lb = {"a": [], "b": [], "c": []}
    for s in D:
        r2 = FITS[(s, key)]["r2"]

Alignment of the spectrogram and the HFB¶

The verifier asked whether the low STRF-R count comes from a misalignment of the stimulus and the neural signal. The MIDDLE eSTRF is refit (best ridge value per electrode, Speech-R electrodes) with the spectrogram read up to 0.5 s earlier (negative shift) or later than the HFB, against the same HFB samples; the segment is padded with its edge values where the shift runs past it. A misaligned audio track would move the best R2 away from 0. Below are also the time at which the mean spectrogram and the mean evoked HFB (Speech-R, MIDDLE) reach half their rise, the ratio of the spectrogram before onset to after it (audio that is not silent before the sound), and the distribution of the MIDDLE model's held-out R2 (adopted ridge value) per subject. The cell after looks for clock drift over the session: it splits each subject's MIDDLE trials by onset into two halves and searches the shift in each over -1 to +1 s.

# Alignment of spectrogram and HFB: held-out R2 of the MIDDLE eSTRF (best ridge value per
# electrode) when the spectrogram is read up to 0.5 s earlier or later against the same HFB.
t0 = time.time()
SHIFTS = np.arange(-25, 26, 5)
rows = []
for s, d in D.items():
    sr = E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "speech_r"].to_numpy()
    idx = cond_idx(d["trials"], "mid")
    for sh in SHIFTS:
        Xs, ys = ac4.trial_design(d, idx, xshift=int(sh))
        _, r2 = ac4.ridge_loto(Xs, [y[:, sr] for y in ys], ALPHAS)
        m = r2.mean(0).max(0)
        rows.append(dict(subject=s, shift_s=sh / ac4.FS_OUT, median_r2=np.median(m), max_r2=m.max(), n_r2_pos=int((m > 0).sum())))
SH = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("spectrogram read later by shift_s (s); Speech-R electrodes, best ridge value per electrode")
for col in ["max_r2", "median_r2", "n_r2_pos"]:
    print(col); print(SH.pivot(index="shift_s", columns="subject", values=col).round(3).to_string())
print("shift with the highest median R2 per subject:", SH.loc[SH.groupby("subject").median_r2.idxmax(), ["subject", "shift_s"]].set_index("subject").shift_s.to_dict())
print(f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
# onset of the spectrogram and of the evoked HFB (Speech-R mean, MIDDLE trials), time of half rise
rows = []
for s, d in D.items():
    idx = cond_idx(d["trials"], "mid")
    sp = np.stack([d["spec"][i][:, :75].mean(0) for i in idx]).mean(0)
    ts = np.arange(75) / ac4.FS_OUT - 0.5
    ep, times = EP[s]
    sr = E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "speech_r"].to_numpy()
    h = ac4.zscore_epochs(d, ep, times, MAIN[0])[idx][:, sr].mean((0, 1))
    half = lambda t, v, b: t[np.argmax(v > v[b].mean() + 0.5 * (v.max() - v[b].mean()))]
    rows.append(dict(subject=s, spec_half_rise_s=half(ts, sp, (ts > -0.45) & (ts < -0.1)),
                     hfb_half_rise_s=half(times, h, (times > -0.5) & (times < -0.1)),
                     spec_pre_over_post=sp[(ts > -0.45) & (ts < 0)].mean() / sp[(ts >= 0) & (ts < 0.5)].mean(),
                     hfb_peak_z=h[(times >= 0) & (times < 1)].max()))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).to_string())
# distribution of the MIDDLE model's held-out R2 (adopted ridge value, mean over splits) per subject
q = E.groupby("subject").mid_r2.describe(percentiles=[0.5, 0.9])[["count", "min", "50%", "90%", "max"]]
q["speech_r_median"] = E[E.speech_r].groupby("subject").mid_r2.median()
q["n_r2_pos"] = E.groupby("subject").mid_r2.apply(lambda v: int((v > 0).sum()))
print(q.round(3).to_string())

# Drift check (verifier, round 2): a fixed offset per subject is tested above; a clock that
# drifts over the session would move the best shift between early and late trials. The MIDDLE
# trials of each subject are split by onset into a first and a second half, and the shift is
# searched over -1 to +1 s in each half (the grid above reaches -0.5 s, where S07's best lies).
t0 = time.time()
SHIFTS_D = np.arange(-50, 51, 5)
rows = []
for s, d in D.items():
    sr = E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "speech_r"].to_numpy()
    idx = cond_idx(d["trials"], "mid")
    idx = idx[np.argsort(d["trials"].onset.to_numpy()[idx])]
    halves = {"first": idx[:len(idx) // 2], "second": idx[len(idx) // 2:], "all": idx}
    for half, hidx in halves.items():
        for sh in SHIFTS_D:
            if half == "all" and abs(sh) <= 25:
                continue                                  # computed in the grid above
            Xs, ys = ac4.trial_design(d, hidx, xshift=int(sh))
            _, r2 = ac4.ridge_loto(Xs, [y[:, sr] for y in ys], ALPHAS)
            m = r2.mean(0).max(0)
            rows.append(dict(subject=s, half=half, n_trials=len(hidx), shift_s=sh / ac4.FS_OUT,
                             median_r2=np.median(m), n_r2_pos=int((m > 0).sum())))
SD = pd.concat([pd.DataFrame(rows), SH.assign(half="all", n_trials=np.nan)[["subject", "half", "n_trials", "shift_s", "median_r2", "n_r2_pos"]]])
SDr = SD.sort_values(["subject", "half", "shift_s"]).reset_index(drop=True)
best_sh = SDr.loc[SDr.groupby(["subject", "half"]).median_r2.idxmax()]
print("shift (s) with the highest median R2, and that R2, per subject and half of the MIDDLE trials (grid -1 to +1 s):")
print(best_sh.pivot(index="subject", columns="half", values="shift_s").to_string())
print(best_sh.pivot(index="subject", columns="half", values="median_r2").round(3).to_string())
print("largest number of Speech-R electrodes with held-out R2 > 0 at any shift:")
print(SDr.groupby(["subject", "half"]).n_r2_pos.max().unstack().to_string())
print(f"{time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

Result: strf-r-count. The MIDDLE eSTRFs predict held-out trials in few electrodes: 9 electrodes are STRF-R under the bootstrap bound (13 with samples to 400 ms after offset), and 0 or 1 under the per-split percentiles, against the paper's 53. Their mean held-out R2 ranges from 0.044 to 0.226, and they come from S01 (4), S02 (1) and S04 (4). Not reproduced.

The alignment check does not point to a misaligned stimulus. In S01 and S04, where the models work, the best R2 lies within 0.1 s of no shift (S01 best median at -0.1 s, S04 at 0 s; the largest R2 at -0.1 to +0.2 s), and the evoked HFB reaches half its rise 0.1 to 0.16 s after the spectrogram. In S03, S07 and S13 no shift from -0.5 to +0.5 s gives any Speech-R electrode a positive held-out R2, and in S02 and S08 at most 3 electrodes at any shift, so no single offset would raise the count. Two subject features bear on the failure: the audio of S02, S04, S07 and S13 is not silent before the sounds (spectrogram before onset 0.43 to 0.66 of that after), and S03's evoked HFB is weak (peak 0.22 z, against 0.65 to 1.35 z elsewhere). In S08 the HFB reaches half its rise 0.06 s before the spectrogram does, which could mean its audio track is a little late, but no shift raises its R2 count above 3. The median held-out R2 of Speech-R electrodes is below 0 in six of seven subjects. The paper's Figure 6b plots mean model scores that are all near or above 0 (most non-included electrodes near 0.07), while most scores here are negative, which suggests a different score; this is asked of the paper's authors.

The drift check finds no drift that would explain the count. In S01, S02, S04 and S13 the best shift is the same in both halves of the MIDDLE trials (-0.1, 0, 0 and 0 s). It differs between halves in S03 (-0.7 and 0 s), S07 (-0.7 and 0 s) and S08 (0 and -0.4 s), but in these subjects no shift in either half gives more than 4 Speech-R electrodes a positive held-out R2 (S07 none), and the median R2 at the best shift is below 0 in every half, so there the best shift is the maximum of a curve without a working model. On the grid widened to -1 s, S07's best median R2 over all trials lies at -0.6 s, still with no electrode above 0.

Result: supp3a-pink-noise-no-hfb-change. On the pink noise triplets, no cluster of AFTER minus BEFORE reaches P < 0.05 over the 36 Speech-R electrodes of S07, S08 and S13 (smallest P = 0.0895), so the claim of absence is reproduced on set (b). Set (a) is empty: none of these subjects' electrodes is included in the eSTRF analyses here. The mean AFTER minus BEFORE difference over 0 to 3 s is nearly the same in pink noise and speech triplets (0.040913 and 0.041035 z, s.e. 0.019 and 0.017), from different time courses (largest difference 1.54 z, correlation of the electrode means 0.61), so the equality is a coincidence of the averages and not a shared array. The speech triplets of the same electrodes do give a significant cluster at 0.50 to 0.74 s (P = 0.0013), with about as many triplets per subject (29 against 28) and the same mean and s.e. over 0 to 3 s, so the difference between the two lies in the time course of the effect, not in the amount of data or the mean.

MTF of eSTRFs against filter type¶

fig8-mtf-matches-filter: the MTFs of the eSTRFs match the filter type of the stimuli they were fit on, in BEFORE, AFTER and in the AFTER minus BEFORE shift.

eSTRFs fit apart on temporal-filtered and spectral-filtered triplets (Figure 8 legend), the MTF as the amplitude of the 2-D FFT of the mean eSTRF (32 bands x 21 lags), the temporal minus spectral MTF difference per included electrode, and MNE's cluster permutation test over the modulation plane (the half plane of non-negative spectral modulation; the amplitude spectrum of a real eSTRF is symmetric). The criterion's region test: a positive cluster (temporal-filter MTF higher) must lie at low temporal and high spectral modulation, a negative one at high temporal and low spectral modulation; "low" and "high" are taken here as below and above the median of the plane's absolute modulations, measured at the cluster's centre (mean over its bins). A second rule takes the regions from the filter cutoffs (Methods, Filtered speech sound creation: 3 Hz, 0.5 cycles/kHz): a cluster is in region when more than half its bins lie at temporal modulation at most 3 Hz and spectral modulation above the cutoff (temporal filter), or the reverse (spectral filter). The spectral axis here is in cycles per band, so 0.5 cycles/kHz is converted at the mean band spacing (0.11 cycles per band); bands are ERB-spaced, so this is an approximation.

In [17]:
inc = E.included.to_numpy()
def strf_of(s, key, ch):
    return FITS[(s, key)]["mean"][:, ch]
tm = np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fftfreq(ac4.MAX_LAG + 1, 1 / ac4.FS_OUT))      # Hz
sm = np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fftfreq(ac4.N_BANDS, 1.0))                     # cycles per band
half = sm >= 0
def mtf_diffs(kind):
    out = []
    for s in D:
        chs = np.where(E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "included"].to_numpy())[0]
        for c in chs:
            if kind in ("bef", "aft"):
                mt = ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, f"{kind}_temp", c)); ms = ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, f"{kind}_freq", c))
            elif kind == "shift_a":    # MTF of the AFTER minus BEFORE eSTRF
                mt = ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, "aft_temp", c) - strf_of(s, "bef_temp", c))
                ms = ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, "aft_freq", c) - strf_of(s, "bef_freq", c))
            else:                      # difference of MTFs
                mt = ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, "aft_temp", c)) - ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, "bef_temp", c))
                ms = ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, "aft_freq", c)) - ac4.mtf(strf_of(s, "bef_freq", c))
            out.append((mt - ms)[half])
    return np.array(out)
TMg, SMg = np.meshgrid(np.abs(tm), sm[half])
med_t, med_s = np.median(TMg), np.median(SMg)
# Second rule, from the filter cutoffs (Methods, Filtered speech sound creation): temporal
# modulations below 3 Hz, spectral modulations below 0.5 cycles/kHz. The spectral axis here is in
# cycles per band; at the mean band spacing (6.82 kHz over 31 steps) 0.5 cycles/kHz is
# 0.11 cycles per band. Low = at or below the cutoff, high = above it.
CUT_T, CUT_S = 3.0, 0.5 * (ac4.F_HI - ac4.F_LO) / 1000 / (ac4.N_BANDS - 1)
kept_t = (TMg <= CUT_T) & (SMg > CUT_S)       # kept by the temporal filter, removed by the spectral
kept_s = (TMg > CUT_T) & (SMg <= CUT_S)       # kept by the spectral filter, removed by the temporal
rows = []
for kind in ["bef", "aft", "shift_a", "shift_b"]:
    X = mtf_diffs(kind)
    T, clusters, pv = clusters_of(X, 8)
    for c, p in zip(clusters, pv):
        sign = "+" if T[c].mean() > 0 else "-"
        ct, cs = TMg[c].mean(), SMg[c].mean()
        match = (sign == "+" and ct < med_t and cs > med_s) or (sign == "-" and ct > med_t and cs < med_s)
        region = kept_t if sign == "+" else kept_s
        rows.append(dict(kind=kind, n=len(X), p=p, sign=sign, bins=int(c.sum()), centre_temporal_Hz=ct,
                         centre_spectral_cyc_per_band=cs, in_region_median_rule=match,
                         frac_bins_in_region_cutoff_rule=(c & region).sum() / c.sum(),
                         in_region_cutoff_rule=(c & region).sum() / c.sum() > 0.5))
    if not len(clusters):
        rows.append(dict(kind=kind, n=len(X), p=np.nan, sign="none"))
R8 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"median rule: |temporal modulation| {med_t:.2f} Hz, spectral modulation {med_s:.3f} cycles/band")
print(f"cutoff rule: temporal {CUT_T} Hz, spectral {CUT_S:.3f} cycles/band; bins kept by the temporal filter only {int(kept_t.sum())}, by the spectral filter only {int(kept_s.sum())}, of {kept_t.size}")
print(R8.sort_values(["kind", "p"]).to_string())
sig = R8[R8.p < 0.05]
print("significant clusters in region, per kind (median rule / cutoff rule):")
print(sig.groupby("kind")[["in_region_median_rule", "in_region_cutoff_rule"]].sum().reindex(["bef", "aft", "shift_a", "shift_b"]).fillna(0).astype(int).to_string())

Result: fig8-mtf-matches-filter. With 9 electrodes, the temporal minus spectral MTF difference has one significant positive cluster in the region the temporal filter keeps in BEFORE (centre 2.1 Hz, P = 0.0078) and two in AFTER under the cutoff rule (1.6 Hz, P = 0.031; 2.0 Hz, P = 0.043), one of which also passes the median rule. Most significant clusters lie outside both regions, at 16 to 19 Hz (BEFORE P = 0.0039 to 0.027, AFTER P = 0.016 to 0.027). For the AFTER minus BEFORE shift, the only significant cluster (P = 0.0039, the smallest P possible with 9 electrodes) lies at 15.3 Hz, outside the regions, with the MTF of the difference, and no cluster reaches P < 0.05 with the difference of MTFs. The criterion asks for an in-region cluster in each of BEFORE, AFTER and the shift; the shift, which carries the claim's conclusion about the tuning change, has none under either rule. Not reproduced.

rng = np.random.default_rng(909)
rows = []
for strf_kind in ["mean", "z"]:
    for rms_kind in ["concat", "per_sound"]:
        diffs, befs = [], []
        for s, d in D.items():
            chs = np.where(E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "included"].to_numpy())[0]
            if not len(chs):
                continue
            Xs, _ = ac4.trial_design(d, cond_idx(d["trials"], "mid"))
            Xa = np.concatenate(Xs)
            mu, sd = Xa.mean(0), Xa.std(0)
            for c in chs:
                v = {}
                for ph in ["bef", "aft"]:
                    w = FITS[(s, ph)][strf_kind][:, c]
                    w = (w - w.mean()) / w.std()
                    if rms_kind == "concat":
                        v[ph] = np.sqrt(np.mean((((Xa - mu) / sd) @ w) ** 2))
                    else:
                        v[ph] = np.mean([np.sqrt(np.mean((((X - mu) / sd) @ w) ** 2)) for X in Xs])
                diffs.append(v["aft"] - v["bef"]); befs.append(v["bef"])
        diffs, befs = np.array(diffs), np.array(befs)
        obs, p = ac4.signflip_test(diffs, rng)
        rows.append(dict(strf=strf_kind, rms=rms_kind, n=len(diffs), rms_before=befs.mean(), relative_increase=(diffs / befs).mean(), mean_increase=obs,
                         se=diffs.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(diffs)), sd=diffs.std(ddof=1), p=p,
                         within_tol=abs(obs - 0.12) <= 0.03, frac_positive=(diffs > 0).mean()))

Result: fig9-rms-increase. Over the 9 included electrodes, the AFTER eSTRF gives a larger RMS output to unfiltered speech than the BEFORE eSTRF under every reading (mean increase 11.4 to 12.0, 8 of 9 electrodes positive with mean coefficients), with P = 0.034 and 0.031 for mean coefficients and 0.077 and 0.073 for z-scored coefficients. The RMS is about 105 here, against about 4 on the paper's axis, so the increase cannot be compared with 0.12 on the paper's scale; the increase as a fraction of the BEFORE RMS is 0.12 to 0.13, printed for comparison only, as the criterion judges the absolute increase. The direction holds; the stated value does not: partially reproduced. Whether the claims file's absolute tolerance can apply to a quantity whose unit the paper does not give is asked of a reader.

MIDDLE eSTRFs predict AFTER better than BEFORE¶

fig9-middle-generalizes-after: eSTRFs fit on unfiltered speech predict HFB activity better in AFTER than in BEFORE (mean R2 improvement 0.05 plus/minus 0.01, P = 0.0001, n = 41).

Methods, MIDDLE condition coefficients generalization: the MIDDLE eSTRF (mean coefficients) convolved with the BEFORE and AFTER spectrograms, and R2 against the HFB. Spectrograms and HFB of each condition are z-scored by that condition's own statistics (Methods: inputs and outputs z-scored). R2 (a) per trial then averaged, (b) over all trials concatenated.

In [19]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(910)
rows = []
for r2_kind in ["per_trial", "concat"]:
    diffs, vals = [], []
    for s, d in D.items():
        chs = np.where(E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), "included"].to_numpy())[0]
        if not len(chs):
            continue
        W = FITS[(s, "mid")]["mean"][:, chs]
        r = {}
        for ph in ["bef", "aft"]:
            Xs, ys = ac4.trial_design(d, cond_idx(d["trials"], ph))
            Xa, ya = np.concatenate(Xs), np.concatenate(ys)[:, chs]
            mu, sd, my, sy = Xa.mean(0), Xa.std(0), ya.mean(0), ya.std(0)
            if r2_kind == "concat":
                pred = ((Xa - mu) / sd) @ W
                yz = (ya - my) / sy
                r[ph] = 1 - ((yz - pred) ** 2).sum(0) / ((yz - yz.mean(0)) ** 2).sum(0)
            else:
                rr = []
                for X, y in zip(Xs, ys):
                    pred = ((X - mu) / sd) @ W
                    yz = (y[:, chs] - my) / sy
                    rr.append(1 - ((yz - pred) ** 2).sum(0) / ((yz - yz.mean(0)) ** 2).sum(0))
                r[ph] = np.mean(rr, 0)
        diffs.append(r["aft"] - r["bef"]); vals.append(np.column_stack([r["bef"], r["aft"]]))
    diffs = np.concatenate(diffs); vals = np.concatenate(vals)
    obs, p = ac4.signflip_test(diffs, rng)
    rows.append(dict(r2=r2_kind, n=len(diffs), r2_before=vals[:, 0].mean(), r2_after=vals[:, 1].mean(),
                     mean_improvement=obs, se=diffs.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(diffs)), sd=diffs.std(ddof=1),
                     p=p, within_tol=abs(obs - 0.05) <= 0.01, frac_positive=(diffs > 0).mean()))
R9b = pd.DataFrame(rows)

Partial correlation of eSTRFs¶

fig10-partial-correlation: Partial correlations of eSTRFs between AFTER and MIDDLE (controlling for BEFORE) exceed those between BEFORE and MIDDLE (controlling for AFTER), a mean improvement of 0.18 (P = 0.001, n = 41).

Methods, eSTRF linear overlap partial correlation analysis: each eSTRF as the z-score of each coefficient across CV splits; sim(aft, mid) = pcorr(after, middle | before), sim(bef, mid) = pcorr(before, middle | after); sign-flip test of the difference. Regression without (a) and with (b) an intercept.

In [20]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(1010)
def pcorr_table(keys=("bef", "mid", "aft"), mask_col="included", subjects=None):
    rows = []
    for s in (subjects or list(D)):
        chs = np.where(E.loc[E.subject.eq(s), mask_col].to_numpy())[0]
        for c in chs:
            b, m, a = (FITS[(s, k)]["z"][:, c] for k in keys)
            row = dict(subject=s, ch=c)
            for icpt in [False, True]:
                tag = "b" if icpt else "a"
                row[f"aft_mid_{tag}"] = ac4.partial_corr(a, m, b, icpt)
                row[f"bef_mid_{tag}"] = ac4.partial_corr(b, m, a, icpt)
                row[f"diff_{tag}"] = row[f"aft_mid_{tag}"] - row[f"bef_mid_{tag}"]
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Connectivity¶

supp6a-connectivity-increase: HFB amplitude coherence between eSTRF seed electrodes and frontal and temporal target electrodes rises slightly in AFTER against BEFORE (temporal-frontal p = 0.025, temporal-temporal p = 0.043, n = 39).

The criterion takes the seeds to be the included electrodes (9 here). The Supplementary Methods (Inter- and Intra-regional Coherence Analysis) restrict them to included electrodes "located on the temporal lobe, hereafter called Temporal seeds" (6 here); that reading is run as a variant and the difference is asked of a reader. Targets are all other temporal electrodes, or the frontal/premotor electrodes: every frontal-* and premotor-* label, including the inferior ones that the region column counts as perisylvian (90 electrodes; the frontal region alone has 64). Per trial the multitaper coherence of the HFB amplitude ("similar to that described above": the 400 ms windows of Figure 4, here the post-stimulus windows 0 to 2.5 s; NW = 4 as for Figure 4, NW = 2 as a variant), averaged over targets, then over trials, integrated over frequency in bits/s, AFTER minus BEFORE per seed, and MNE's permutation t-test across seeds. With n seeds the smallest P an exact sign-flip test can give is 2 / 2^n (0.0039 for 9, 0.031 for 6).

In [24]:
def seed_coherence(target_region, seed_set="included", nw=4.0, fmin=None):
    """Per seed the mean over post-stimulus windows of the coherence (bits/s) with the targets,
    averaged over targets then trials, for BEFORE, MIDDLE and AFTER."""
    rows = []
    for s, d in D.items():
        g = E[E.subject.eq(s)].reset_index(drop=True)
        seed_mask = g.included if seed_set == "included" else g.included & g.region.eq("temporal")
        seeds = np.where(seed_mask.to_numpy())[0]
        if target_region == "frontal":
            targ_all = np.where(g.description.str.startswith(("frontal", "premotor")).to_numpy())[0]
        else:
            targ_all = np.where(g.region.eq("temporal").to_numpy())[0]
        ep, times = EP[s]
        zep = ac4.zscore_epochs(d, ep, times, MAIN[0])
        tr = d["trials"]
        for c in seeds:
            targ = targ_all[targ_all != c]
            if not len(targ):
                continue
            row = dict(subject=s, seed=c, seed_region=g.region[c], n_targets=len(targ))
            for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]:
                X = zep[cond_idx(tr, ph)]
                bits = []
                for ws in WIN_STARTS[WIN_STARTS >= 0]:
                    sel = (times >= ws - 1e-9) & (times < ws + 0.4 - 1e-9)
                    f, coh = ac4.mt_coherence(X[:, [c]][..., sel], X[:, targ][..., sel], ac4.FS_OUT, nw=nw)
                    bits.append(ac4.coh_to_bits(coh.mean(1), f, fmin=fmin).mean())   # mean over targets, then trials
                row[ph] = np.mean(bits)
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
COH6_ALL, rows = {}, []
for seed_set, fmin in [("included", None), ("temporal included", None), ("included", "W")]:
    for nw in [4.0, 2.0]:
        for reg in ["frontal", "temporal"]:
            t = seed_coherence(reg, seed_set, nw, None if fmin is None else nw / 0.4)
            label = seed_set if fmin is None else f"{seed_set}, from {nw / 0.4:g} Hz"
            COH6_ALL[(label, nw, reg)] = t
            diff = (t.aft - t.bef).to_numpy()
            T, p, _ = mne.stats.permutation_t_test(diff[:, None], n_permutations=10000, seed=6, tail=0)
            rows.append(dict(seeds=label, NW=nw, targets=reg, n_seeds=len(t), subjects=t.subject.nunique(),
                             bef=t.bef.mean(), mid=t.mid.mean(), aft=t.aft.mean(), aft_minus_bef=diff.mean(),
                             positive=int((diff > 0).sum()), t=T[0], p=p[0], min_possible_p=2 / 2 ** len(t)))

Result: supp6a-connectivity-increase. Integrated from 2.5 Hz with the 9 included electrodes as seeds and NW = 4, HFB coherence rises from BEFORE to AFTER with frontal/premotor targets (+0.27 bits/s, 9 of 9 seeds positive, t = 3.96, P = 0.0039) and with temporal targets (+0.25, 7 of 9, t = 2.64, P = 0.039). This result depends on the seeds and the bandwidth as well: with NW = 2 the temporal targets give P = 0.070, and with the 6 temporal seeds of the Supplementary Methods P = 0.094 (NW = 4) and 0.094 (NW = 2), while the frontal targets pass in every variant (P = 0.0039 to 0.031). The seeds come from three subjects.

Integrated from W (10 Hz at NW = 4, 5 Hz at NW = 2), the lowest frequency the tapers resolve apart from 0 Hz, neither target region shows an increase (frontal P = 0.46, temporal P = 0.72 at NW = 4; 0.23 and 0.41 at NW = 2). Of the frontal increase of 0.27 bits/s at NW = 4, 0.05 remains from 10 Hz up, so the effect lies in the bins at 2.5 to 7.5 Hz, whose tapers reach 0 Hz and so carry the slow time course of each window. The claims file's standard choice integrates from the lowest resolved frequency, read here as W, so the claim is not reproduced. The third verification round agreed with this change of outcome (it was reproduced, from 2.5 Hz, in rounds 1 and 2). The outcome rests on reading the lowest resolved frequency as W, which follows from the multitaper bandwidth, and the paper gives neither.

Result: supp6a-after-closer-to-middle. Integrated from 2.5 Hz with the 9 included seeds and NW = 4, for both target regions the AFTER coherence is closer to MIDDLE than BEFORE is: mean |AFTER - MIDDLE| 0.54 against |BEFORE - MIDDLE| 0.82 bits/s for frontal targets (9 of 9 seeds closer), and 0.93 against 1.17 for temporal targets (7 of 9). The 6 temporal seeds give the same at NW = 4 and NW = 2. With 9 seeds at NW = 2 the temporal targets do not (0.204 against 0.182). Integrated from W, the lowest resolved frequency as for supp6a-connectivity-increase, AFTER is not closer to MIDDLE in either region (frontal 0.248 against 0.241, temporal 0.207 against 0.143 at NW = 4; 0.285 against 0.232 and 0.223 against 0.185 at NW = 2), and MIDDLE has the lowest coherence of the three conditions. Not reproduced. The third verification round agreed with this change of outcome (it was reproduced, from 2.5 Hz, in rounds 1 and 2).

supp6b-no-pac-change: Phase-amplitude coupling between 3 to 8 Hz phase in frontal/premotor electrodes and HFB amplitude in the eSTRF electrodes does not change from BEFORE to AFTER.

Supplementary Methods, Theta Connectivity Phase-Amplitude Coupling Analysis: phase from 3 to 10 Hz in 0.5 Hz steps (band-pass of +/- 1 Hz around each, a standard choice) on the frontal/premotor electrodes, HFB amplitude from 10 log-spaced bands 70 to 140 Hz on the included electrodes, the post-stimulus samples (onset to sound end) concatenated over trials per condition, PAC as in Ozkurt and Schnitzler (2011), averaged over phases 3 to 8 Hz (variants 4 to 8 and 2 to 12 Hz, the legend's), then over phase electrodes other than the amplitude electrode itself (one included electrode is also a frontal/premotor phase electrode); AFTER minus BEFORE; permutation t-test against 0.

In [26]:
PH_F = np.arange(2.0, 12.01, 0.5)
def ozkurt(amp, ph):
    n = amp.shape[-1]
    return np.abs((amp * np.exp(1j * ph)).sum(-1)) / (np.sqrt(n) * np.sqrt((amp ** 2).sum(-1)))
rows = []
for s, d in D.items():
    g = E[E.subject.eq(s)].reset_index(drop=True)
    amp_ch = np.where(g.included.to_numpy())[0]
    ph_ch = np.where(g.description.str.startswith(("frontal", "premotor")).to_numpy())[0]
    if not len(amp_ch) or not len(ph_ch):
        continue
    tr = d["trials"]
    t_ep = np.arange(int(ac4.EPOCH[0] * ac4.FS), int(ac4.EPOCH[1] * ac4.FS)) / ac4.FS
    res = {}
    for ph in ["bef", "aft"]:
        idx = cond_idx(tr, ph)
        raw = d["raw_ep"][idx].astype(np.float64)
        amp = ac4.hfb_amplitude(raw[:, amp_ch], np.geomspace(70, 140, 10))
        phases = np.stack([ac4.band_phase(raw[:, ph_ch], f - 1, f + 1) for f in PH_F])  # (freq, trials, ch, t)
        masks = [(t_ep >= 0) & (t_ep < dur) for dur in tr.duration.to_numpy()[idx]]
        A = np.concatenate([amp[i][:, m] for i, m in enumerate(masks)], axis=-1)          # (amp_ch, samples)
        P = np.concatenate([phases[:, i][..., m] for i, m in enumerate(masks)], axis=-1)  # (freq, ph_ch, samples)
        res[ph] = ozkurt(A[None, None], P[:, :, None])                                    # (freq, ph_ch, amp_ch)
    for j, c in enumerate(amp_ch):
        others = ph_ch != c            # an included frontal electrode is not its own phase electrode
        row = dict(subject=s, ch=c, n_phase_ch=int(others.sum()), self_excluded=bool((~others).any()))
        for lab, lo, hi in [("3-8", 3, 8), ("4-8", 4, 8), ("2-12", 2, 12)]:
            fm = (PH_F >= lo) & (PH_F <= hi)
            row[f"bef_{lab}"] = res["bef"][fm][:, others, j].mean()
            row[f"aft_{lab}"] = res["aft"][fm][:, others, j].mean()
        rows.append(row)
PAC = pd.DataFrame(rows)
for lab in ["3-8", "4-8", "2-12"]:
    diff = (PAC[f"aft_{lab}"] - PAC[f"bef_{lab}"]).to_numpy()
    T, p, _ = mne.stats.permutation_t_test(diff[:, None], n_permutations=10000, seed=7, tail=0)
    print(f"phase {lab} Hz: n = {len(diff)} amplitude electrodes ({PAC.subject.nunique()} subjects), BEFORE {PAC[f'bef_{lab}'].mean():.4f}, AFTER {PAC[f'aft_{lab}'].mean():.4f}, AFTER-BEFORE {diff.mean():.5f}, t = {T[0]:.2f}, P = {p[0]:.4f}")
print("amplitude electrodes that are also phase electrodes (left out of their own mean):", int(PAC.self_excluded.sum()))

Result: supp6b-no-pac-change. PAC between 3 to 8 Hz frontal/premotor phase and HFB amplitude of the 9 included electrodes does not change from BEFORE to AFTER (difference 0.00057, t = 1.60, P = 0.14); the variants give P = 0.063 (4 to 8 Hz) and 0.52 (2 to 12 Hz). With 9 electrodes the test has little power, and the 4 to 8 Hz variant is near the bound. Reproduced.

Coherence with the speech envelope¶

supp7-envelope-coherence: In temporal electrodes, theta coherence with the speech envelope is higher for unfiltered speech than for BEFORE (p = 0.001, n = 72), but does not differ between BEFORE and AFTER; frontal electrodes show no effects.

Supplementary Methods and Supplementary Figure 7: the speech envelope from 64 log-spaced wavelets 500 to 2000 Hz, rectified and averaged; multitaper coherence of the re-referenced ECoG with the envelope over 0 to 3 s per trial (both resampled to 100 Hz; jackknife; NW = 4, seven tapers, MNE's default as for Figure 4, and NW = 3, five tapers, the first revision's choice, as a variant), converted to normal mutual information per frequency (-log2(1 - coh)), averaged over trials; the MIDDLE minus BEFORE and AFTER minus BEFORE differences per frequency, and MNE's cluster permutation test over frequency (1 to 30 Hz) across the Speech-R electrodes of the temporal lobe and of frontal/premotor cortex.

In [27]:
import scipy.signal as ss
def envelope_nmi(nw):
  NMI = []
  for s, d in D.items():
      tr = d["trials"]
      t_ep = np.arange(int(ac4.EPOCH[0] * ac4.FS), int(ac4.EPOCH[1] * ac4.FS)) / ac4.FS
      sel = (t_ep >= 0) & (t_ep < 3.0)
      out = {}
      for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]:
          idx = cond_idx(tr, ph)
          x = ss.resample_poly(d["raw_ep"][idx][..., sel].astype(np.float64), 1, 10, axis=-1)       # (trials, ch, 300)
          env = np.stack([ss.resample_poly(d["env"][i][:3000], 1, 10) for i in idx])                # (trials, 300)
          f, coh = ac4.mt_coherence(x, np.broadcast_to(env[:, None], x.shape), 100.0, nw=nw)
          out[ph] = (-np.log2(1 - np.clip(coh, 0, 1 - 1e-9))).mean(0)                                # (ch, freqs)
      NMI.append(out)
  return {ph: np.concatenate([o[ph] for o in NMI]) for ph in ["bef", "mid", "aft"]}, f
NMI_NW = {nw: envelope_nmi(nw) for nw in [4.0, 3.0]}
NMI, f = NMI_NW[4.0]
fsel = (f >= 1) & (f <= 30)
print("frequencies tested:", f[fsel])
groups = {"temporal": (E.speech_r & E.region.eq("temporal")).to_numpy(),
          "frontal": (E.speech_r & E.description.str.startswith(("frontal", "premotor"))).to_numpy()}
rows = []
for nw, (NMI_, _) in NMI_NW.items():
  for gname, m in groups.items():
    for comp in ["mid", "aft"]:
        X = (NMI_[comp] - NMI_["bef"])[m][:, fsel]
        if len(X) < 3:
            rows.append(dict(NW=nw, electrodes=gname, comparison=f"{comp}-bef", n=len(X), p=np.nan, sign="too few"))
            continue
        T, clusters, pv = clusters_of(X, 77)
        if not len(clusters):
            rows.append(dict(NW=nw, electrodes=gname, comparison=f"{comp}-bef", n=len(X), p=np.nan, sign="no cluster"))
        for c, p in zip(clusters, pv):
            fc = f[fsel][c]
            rows.append(dict(NW=nw, electrodes=gname, comparison=f"{comp}-bef", n=len(X), p=p, sign="+" if T[c].mean() > 0 else "-",
                             f_lo=fc.min(), f_hi=fc.max(), overlaps_3_8=(fc.min() <= 8) and (fc.max() >= 3),
                             overlaps_2_12=(fc.min() <= 12) and (fc.max() >= 2)))
R7 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(R7.to_string())
for gname, m in groups.items():
    th = (f >= 3) & (f <= 8)
    print(f"{gname} Speech-R (n = {m.sum()}): mean NMI 3-8 Hz BEFORE {NMI['bef'][m][:, th].mean():.4f}, MIDDLE {NMI['mid'][m][:, th].mean():.4f}, AFTER {NMI['aft'][m][:, th].mean():.4f} bits")

Result: supp7-envelope-coherence. With NW = 4, in the 66 temporal Speech-R electrodes, MIDDLE minus BEFORE envelope coherence has positive clusters at 7.3 to 8.7 Hz (P = 0.012) and 1.3 to 2.3 Hz (P = 0.037), overlapping the 3 to 8 Hz and 2 to 12 Hz theta ranges; no AFTER minus BEFORE cluster reaches P < 0.05 (smallest 0.095); in the 19 frontal/premotor Speech-R electrodes no cluster of either test reaches P < 0.05 (smallest 0.081). Mean NMI from 3 to 8 Hz in temporal electrodes is 0.139 BEFORE, 0.154 MIDDLE and 0.141 AFTER bits. Reproduced under NW = 4, with the theta cluster at the upper edge of 3 to 8 Hz. With NW = 3 it is not: no temporal MIDDLE minus BEFORE cluster reaches P < 0.05 (smallest 0.093, 1.7 to 2.3 Hz), and the frontal electrodes show MIDDLE above BEFORE at 6.7 to 8.3 Hz (P = 0.0012). The outcome rests on the bandwidth, which the paper does not give.

HFB power by wavelets¶

supp4-hfb-power-increase: Power in the HFB range rises in AFTER against BEFORE in frontal (p = 0.001, n = 75) and temporal (p = 0.002, n = 217) electrodes, and power below 25 Hz falls in frontal electrodes (p = 0.001).

Supplementary Figure 4 legend: 100 log-spaced Morlet wavelets of 5 cycles, post-stimulus power averaged over time, AFTER minus BEFORE, cluster permutation test over frequency across frontal and across temporal electrodes. The claims file's standard choice is 1 to 200 Hz with power in decibels against the -800 to -100 ms baseline; the kept epochs (-1 to 3.5 s) are too short for a 5-cycle wavelet below about 3 Hz, so the range here is 3 to 200 Hz. Below about 10 Hz the wavelets reach the start of the epoch from inside the baseline, so the post-stimulus power alone (dB, no baseline; 0 to 2.5 s ends 1 s before the epoch end) is also tested. Post-stimulus is 0 to 2.5 s (claims, open detail 2, reading b). Frontal electrodes are the frontal-* and premotor-* labels, temporal the temporal lobe labels; all good electrodes.

WF = np.geomspace(3, 200, 100)
POW, POWR = [], []
for s, d in D.items():
    tr = d["trials"]
    t_ep = np.arange(int(ac4.EPOCH[0] * ac4.FS), int(ac4.EPOCH[1] * ac4.FS)) / ac4.FS
    td = t_ep[::10]
    base = (td >= -0.8) & (td <= -0.1)
    post = (td >= 0) & (td <= 2.5)
    out, outr = {}, {}
    for ph in ["bef", "aft"]:
        x = d["raw_ep"][cond_idx(tr, ph)].astype(np.float64)
        acc, accr = [], []
        for fchunk in np.array_split(WF, 10):
            p = mne.time_frequency.tfr_array_morlet(x, ac4.FS, fchunk, n_cycles=5, output="power", decim=10)
            acc.append(10 * np.log10(p[..., post].mean(-1) / p[..., base].mean(-1)).mean(0))     # (ch, f)
            accr.append(10 * np.log10(p[..., post].mean(-1)).mean(0))     # no baseline: post-stimulus power only
        out[ph], outr[ph] = np.concatenate(acc, axis=1), np.concatenate(accr, axis=1)
    POW.append(out["aft"] - out["bef"]); POWR.append(outr["aft"] - outr["bef"])
POW, POWR = np.concatenate(POW), np.concatenate(POWR)
rows = []
for power, PW in [("dB against baseline", POW), ("post-stimulus dB, no baseline", POWR)]:
    for gname, m in [("frontal", E.description.str.startswith(("frontal", "premotor")).to_numpy()), ("temporal", E.region.eq("temporal").to_numpy())]:
        T, clusters, pv = clusters_of(PW[m], 44)
        for c, p in zip(clusters, pv):
            rows.append(dict(power=power, electrodes=gname, n=int(m.sum()), p=p, sign="+" if T[c].mean() > 0 else "-", f_lo=WF[c].min(), f_hi=WF[c].max(),
                             hfb_overlap=(WF[c].max() >= 70) and (WF[c].min() <= 150), below_25=WF[c].min() < 25))
        hf = (WF >= 70) & (WF <= 150)
        print(f"{power}, {gname}: n = {m.sum()}, mean AFTER-BEFORE 70-150 Hz {PW[m][:, hf].mean():.3f} dB, below 25 Hz {PW[m][:, WF < 25].mean():.3f} dB")
R4 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(R4.to_string())

Result: supp4-hfb-power-increase. AFTER minus BEFORE wavelet power has a positive cluster covering the HFB range in frontal/premotor electrodes (26 to 200 Hz, P = 0.0001, n = 90) and in temporal electrodes (51 to 200 Hz, P = 0.0005, n = 192), and a negative cluster below 25 Hz in frontal electrodes (4.2 to 19.4 Hz, P = 0.0001). Without a baseline the three effects remain: HFB increases in frontal (19 to 200 Hz, P = 0.0006) and temporal electrodes (25 to 200 Hz, P = 0.0002) and a frontal decrease at 3.9 to 6.7 Hz (P = 0.034). Reproduced, with electrode counts that differ from the paper's 75 and 217.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's: the HFB band edges, the filter orders, the auditory spectrogram's compression and sharpening and the wavelet range are standard choices the paper does not fix; the multitaper bandwidth is MNE's default (NW = 4), the claims file's standard choice, on which supp6a-connectivity-increase, supp6a-after-closer-to-middle and supp7-envelope-coherence depend; the coherence of Supplementary Figure 6a is integrated from the tapers' half-bandwidth (10 Hz), the lowest resolved frequency, and both supp6a claims are reproduced when it is integrated from 2.5 Hz; Figure 4's claims are reproduced under either bound; the z-score that defines Speech-R is the code's z-score by non-event times, the only one of three readings that gives counts near the paper's; the ridge parameter is the mode of the per-split best values below the top of the grid, since the mode over all values falls at the top of any grid. The eSTRFs predict held-out trials in far fewer electrodes than the paper reports (9 against 53), so every eSTRF claim rests on 9 electrodes from three subjects, and the pink noise eSTRF claim cannot be tested. A check of the alignment of spectrogram and HFB finds no offset, and no drift over the session, that would raise the count.

What was found about the data set: it holds 7 subjects with 416 channels (377 marked good) against the paper's 524 recorded and 468 kept, with no mapping between its subject names and the paper's S1 to S7; the stored values are not in the stated millivolts and their scale differs by six orders of magnitude between S01 and the other subjects; the behavioural control data are not included; the stimulus audio is included although the data set's own notebook says it is not; events marked bad are not described.
